result.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone. Removal is exact within each layer; as with key-value eviction in attention, expired frames can retain residual influence through the cached inputs computed by earlier layers. We design a dedicated data structure and GPU kernels to achieve low caching and composition overhead. Across five open-source hybrid VLMs and four video reasoning benchmarks, Spool achieves the lowest p95 time-to-first-token in all 20 model-benchmark tests, reducing it by a geometric mean of $6.6\times$ over the faster of two recent vLLM baselines, while improving accuracy by 2.3 percentage points on average.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Spool：注意到混合 VLM 中线性循环层对状态的更新是仿射且可结合复合的，于是缓存每帧的状态变换，在滑动窗口推进时无需重放帧即可精确移除过期帧，实现免训练的低延迟流式视频推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 「按帧可组合的仿射状态变换」为在 latent 状态中有选择地保留或剔除视觉证据提供了机制线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中的证据筛选与状态内容保持问题；但原文仅评测时延与准确率，未涉及推理过程分析，迁移需进一步核查。
